scope: Measured approaching lane hulls versus stationary-obstacle braking
reference_ranges: HBQ driveAssist oncoming-priority branch1083-1104 and closest-relative-approach context1105-1125; queue/back-up context1383-1515. Scoped comparison, not whole-controller review.
reference_disposition: HBQ distinguishes oncoming traffic and relative approach. Its ID-ranked one-sided wait, public timestamp queue request and forced-physics pushes do not supply CBE bilateral consent or native queue execution. These methods were not copied.
finding: CBE retained lane hull occupancy but set the non-following forward-speed allowance to zero. Its closing calculation consequently modeled an oncoming/reversing hull as stationary, omitting approach during own reaction and braking.
change: For measured longitudinal approach above0.5m/s, constrain existing cap by v*T+v^2/(2a)+u*(T+v/a)<=available room. If actual-speed modeled stopping room is already consumed, cap is zero. No discovery query, route write, peer command or consent is added. Existing ordinary/convoy consumers remain the sole writers.

validation.numerical: Independent constant-approach equation checks over3 decelerations,5 room values and4 approaching speeds; allowance never exceeds stationary model; infeasible reaction room requires zero.
validation.fixture: Normal-only opposing native MOVE trucks require real overlapping-lane closing, peer approach and opposite headings, live production observation, actual3km/h reduction, eight-corner hull separation and no damage. No cap/callback/result injection. PREPARED_NOT_RUN.

limits: No physical braking, driver reaction, peer acceleration, native steering or overhead acceptance.
Stopping this vehicle cannot stop an uncooperative approaching peer or guarantee no eventual collision.
HBQ queue-cascade and bilateral jam-resolution operation remain unimplemented; no queue-clear claim.
Sampling horizon, unusually fast or large modded vehicles and dense discovery budgets remain limitations.
